the_ranking_is_model_independent.reading: both groupings work under both model families, both beat the random grouping significantly, and pathway beats target in both. The gap is slightly smaller under the tree but clearly resolvable (MDE 0.0335 against an effect of 0.0572).

this_forces_a_correction_to_C106.what_C106_said: under boosting the coarsening does not substitute for a missing identity (the tree reached only about 0.032)
this_forces_a_correction_to_C106.what_this_round_shows: with the grouping as the only input the tree reaches 0.1074, close to ridge's 0.1254
this_forces_a_correction_to_C106.the_likely_cause: R138's tree carried the drug identity codes, all of which were the reserved code -1 on the evaluation rows. That is a dead feature which consumes splits and distorts the routing, so the tree was handicapped by the encoding rather than by its model family.
this_forces_a_correction_to_C106.how_I_found_it: the first attempt of this very round had the same defect: with integer drug codes fed to the tree, 'identity' scored 0.081 in a condition where identity can carry no information. Removing the dead feature fixed both problems.
this_forces_a_correction_to_C106.status_of_C106: must be re-tested with grouping-only features on both sides before it can be quoted again

the_pattern_that_keeps_recurring.class: a feature that carries no information in the evaluation condition still changes what a flexible model does
instances: R135 one_seen_only: in-sample, two arms numerically identical
R144: marginal arm constant when both drugs unseen
R147 first attempt: integer identity codes give held-out drugs arbitrary scores, identity 'scoring' 0.081
R138, now suspected: the dead identity block handicaps the tree's use of the grouping
the_pattern_that_keeps_recurring.rule: before comparing arms, check that every feature present in every arm actually carries information in the evaluation condition
